title: mgmt.transport Facet
description: How an Entity is REACHED — the peer of mgmt.address, which says where (ADR-0156, extending ADR-0084). Written by the Syncer that observed the host, with provenance (§1.2): kubecompute observes `kubectl`, vcenter observes `vmware_tools`, awsec2 observes `aws_ssm` or `ssh`. Multi-writer by design and already precedented — mgmt.address is written by the declared-estate Syncer, the vcenter Syncer and build project-backs alike, under cross-source per-key Facet ownership (ADR-0041/0042). IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE CONNECTION METHOD IS A PROPERTY OF THE SUBSTRATE, NOT OF THE STEP. Every substrate ships a native Ansible connection plugin and none of them uses SSH: kubernetes.core.kubectl needs NOTHING in the guest, community.vmware.vmware_tools goes through vCenter's guest-operations API and needs no network path to the guest at all, amazon.aws.aws_ssm goes through an SSM Session. Declaring the transport on the Step would force a converge Workflow to name a substrate — precisely what ADR-0151 removed from every declaration above the provider — and would make a MIXED-SUBSTRATE View unconvergeable, because connection settings rendered as inventory group vars are one value for the whole Run. Observed here instead, the shim renders per-HOST vars and one Assignment converges pods, VMs and EC2 instances in ONE Run, naming none of them. COORDINATES, NEVER CREDENTIALS (§2.5, ADR-0084 D4's split applied to the transport): this carries what IDENTIFIES the target — a pod and namespace, a VM path, an instance id and region — and holds no vCenter password, no guest password, no AWS key and no kubeconfig. Those arrive as brokered CredentialRefs on the Step, resolved at their mount. Core never branches on `kind`; it carries and logs it exactly as it carries the address, which is what keeps the spine from holding a closed set of substrates (§9) while leaving a Run's descent legible (§1.8). `local` is deliberately NOT a kind: a control-node target already declares itself through mgmt.address's reserved value, and a second home for that fact would be resolved by a precedence rule §2.4 refuses. Closed (§9).

kind.description: the connection plugin this target is reached by. `ssh` is an OBSERVATION, not a default — it means the Syncer determined this host is SSH-reachable, which is different from no transport being observed at all.

container.description: kubectl: the container within the pod, when it has more than one

vmPath.description: vmware_tools: the VM's inventory path, e.g. /DC0/vm/web-01

vmUuid.description: vmware_tools: the VM's uuid, when the path is ambiguous

region.description: aws_ssm: the region the instance is in

allOf.$comment: Per-kind coordinate requirements, stated as if/then so a validation failure names the missing field rather than reporting that the document matched no branch (§1.8 — the oneOf-error problem ADR-0153 D4 already hit).
